title: Add graceful shutdown with in‑flight request handling
description: Ensures the framework can terminate cleanly in production by stopping new connections, waiting for ongoing requests to finish, and exiting with proper logging. Prevents abrupt termination that can corrupt data or drop client responses.
testCases: When SIGTERM is received, server stops accepting new connections but continues processing existing ones until they finish or timeout.
If in‑flight requests exceed the configured timeout, they are force‑closed and the process exits with status 0.
acceptance: The server logs "Shutdown initiated", stops listening on the port, waits up to the configured timeout for all active requests, logs "Shutdown complete" and exits. No new requests are accepted after shutdown begins, and all pending requests either complete successfully or are terminated after the timeout.
reason: Production deployments need reliable termination to avoid data loss, improve uptime during rolling updates, and meet SLA requirements for graceful service restarts.
